chapter: Chapter 7 — Memory Is the First Constraint
evidence: PDF p.21: 'Arithmetic belongs on the epistemic-status axis, not the provenance axis: a worked example computed from a model card is [1P][DERIVED], never [2°].' PDF p.22: 'The deployment unit those constants are priced into — an 8×H100 host — is a scenario choice, not a vendor fact: [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION], as Table 4-2 records it.' PDF p.160: '3×H100 total VRAM / 3 ×80 GB = 240 GB / 3 × the vendor’s 80 GB per-part constant [1P] / [FACT] (NVIDIA H100 80 GB specification); like the 2× and 8× rows and the 640 GB pool in Table 7-2, the capacity is a [1P][FACT] vendor constant'
issue: Derived aggregate host-memory capacities are labeled as first-party facts. The 2×/3×/8× H100 totals and the 640 GB pool are arithmetic over a vendor per-part constant plus a scenario-defined host composition, not vendor-stated facts; this contradicts the book's own evidence rules.
fix_instruction: Relabel aggregate capacity rows such as 2×H100, 3×H100, 8×H100, and the 640 GB pool as [1P][DERIVED] from the [1P][FACT] per-GPU VRAM constant, with the host composition tied to [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] where it is used. Sweep the same aggregate-capacity label pattern in Table 7-2 and any later recurrence.
